types.embedding_query_text: Disease: A disorder of structure or function in a human, animal, or plant, especially one that produces specific symptoms or that affects a specific location and is not simply a direct result of physical injury. Also called Illness, Sickness, Malady, Affliction. Examples: Ebola.

chosen_type.label: InfectiousDisease
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Disease' and mention 'Ebola' are best represented by the more specific 'InfectiousDisease' as Ebola is an infectious condition.

candidates.label: Animal
candidates.comment: A living organism that feeds on organic matter, typically having specialized sense organs and nervous system and able to respond rapidly to stimuli.

candidates.label: MedicalCondition
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any condition of the human body that affects normal functioning, including diseases, injuries, disabilities, and disorders. Also called disease, illness, health disorder, ailment. Examples: "influenza", "diabetes", "a broken arm", "depression", "asthma".

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: Disaster
candidates.comment: A sudden event, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe, that causes great damage or loss of life.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory. Also called Nation, State, Land, Realm. Examples: Democratic Republic of Congo, Belgium, UK, Uganda.

chosen_type.label: Country
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Country' directly matches the Schema.org 'Country' class, and all mentions are instances of countries.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: NationalGroup
candidates.comment: A group of people sharing a common nationality.

candidates.label: GovernmentDeclaration
candidates.comment: An official announcement or statement made by a government.

candidates.label: IslandGroup
candidates.comment: A cluster or chain of islands.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose, such as a business, government department, or charity. Also called Association, Institution, Body, Agency. Examples: World Health Organization, Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale, Institute of Tropical Medicine, University of Oxford.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Organization' directly matches the Schema.org 'Organization' class, which is broad enough to cover all mentions.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being. Also called Individual, Human, Man, Woman. Examples: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, Dr Samuel Roger Kamba, pregnant woman, individual.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Person' directly matches the Schema.org 'Person' class, and all mentions are instances of human beings.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: TennisPlayer
candidates.comment: An individual who plays the sport of tennis.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: EnvironmentalPhenomenon
candidates.comment: A natural occurrence or ongoing process related to the environment.

candidates.label: CalendarYear
candidates.comment: A specific calendar year.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: One of the seven days of the week. Also called Weekday, Weekend day. Examples: Thursday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'DayOfWeek' directly matches the Schema.org 'DayOfWeek' enumeration, and 'Thursday' is a perfect instance.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: CalendarYear
candidates.comment: A specific calendar year.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: CalendarSeason
candidates.comment: One of the four divisions of the year (spring, summer, autumn, and winter) marked by particular weather patterns and daylight hours.

types.embedding_query_text: Quantity: A specific amount or number of something. Also called Amount, Number, Count, Total. Examples: 1,400, 438, two, 1,460.

chosen_type.label: Quantity
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Quantity' directly matches the Schema.org 'Quantity' datatype, which represents measurable amounts and numerical values.

candidates.label: Quantity
candidates.comment: Quantity is a data type representing measurable amounts such as distance, time, mass, or weight. Also called amount, measure, magnitude. Examples: '3 kg', '4 milligrams', '10 meters', '2 hours'.

candidates.label: Mass
candidates.comment: A quantity representing the amount of matter in an object, typically expressed with a unit of measure. Also called weight, bulk, quantity of matter. Examples: "5 kg", "10 pounds", "200 grams", "1 ton". Distinct from Quantity, which is a broader concept for any measurable amount.

candidates.label: Number
candidates.comment: Number is a data type representing numerical values. Also called numeric value, quantity, digit. Examples: 10, 3.14, -5, 1000000. Distinct from Text, which represents character strings.

candidates.label: Rate
candidates.comment: A measure of a quantity or frequency, typically expressed as a ratio of one quantity to another.

candidates.label: Temperature
candidates.comment: A measure of the degree of hotness or coldness of a substance or environment.

types.embedding_query_text: VirusSpecies: A specific classification of a virus, often characterized by its genetic makeup and host range. Also called Viral strain, Virus type. Examples: Bundibugyo virus.

chosen_type.label: VirusSpecies
chosen_type.definition: A specific biological classification of a virus, characterized by its genetic makeup and host range.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate precisely captures 'VirusSpecies'; 'Taxon' is a suitable parent but too broad for the specific OIE type.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

candidates.label: InfectiousDisease
candidates.comment: An InfectiousDisease is a medical condition resulting from the presence of pathogenic microbial agents like viruses, bacteria, or fungi. Also called communicable disease, contagious illness, infection. Examples: influenza, COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis. Distinct from MedicalCondition, which is a broader category for any health problem.

candidates.label: Gene
candidates.comment: A Gene is a BioChemEntity representing a discrete unit of inheritance that affects one or more biological traits. Also called genetic unit, hereditary factor. Examples: FOXP2, SCARNA21, the gene for eye color, a specific allele.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: MusicAlbumProductionType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumProductionType is an enumeration classifying a music album by its content type. Also called album type, production category. Examples: StudioAlbum, LiveAlbum, Soundtrack, CompilationAlbum. Distinct from MusicAlbumReleaseType, which describes the release format.

types.embedding_query_text: DrugClass: A group of drugs that have similar chemical structures, the same mechanism of action, and are used to treat the same disease. Also called Medication category, Pharmaceutical class. Examples: antiviral drugs.

chosen_type.label: DrugClass
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'DrugClass' directly matches the Schema.org 'DrugClass' class, and 'antiviral drugs' is a perfect instance.

candidates.label: DrugClass
candidates.comment: A DrugClass is a MedicalEntity representing a category of medical drugs, grouped by general pharmacological class, common mechanisms of action, or physiological effects. Also called drug category, medication group, therapeutic class. Examples: Statins, Antibiotics, Antidepressants, Beta-blockers.

candidates.label: Drug
candidates.comment: A Drug is a Product that is a chemical or biological substance used as a medical therapy, having a physiological effect on an organism. Also called medicine, pharmaceutical, medication. Examples: Aspirin, Insulin, Penicillin, Ibuprofen.

candidates.label: InfectiousAgentClass
candidates.comment: InfectiousAgentClass is a medical enumeration of classes of agents or pathogens that transmit infectious diseases. Also called pathogen type, disease agent category, microbial class. Examples: 'Bacteria', 'Virus', 'Fungus', 'Parasite'.

candidates.label: DrugStrength
candidates.comment: A DrugStrength is a MedicalIntangible representing a specific potency in which a medical drug is available in a particular country. Also called medication dosage, pharmaceutical concentration. Examples: "500 mg tablets", "10 mg/mL solution", "25 mcg patch".

candidates.label: DrugPregnancyCategory
candidates.comment: A DrugPregnancyCategory is a MedicalEnumeration assessing the risk of fetal injury from a drug used by the mother during pregnancy. Also called pregnancy risk category, fetal risk classification. Examples: PregnancyCategoryA, PregnancyCategoryX, PregnancyCategoryD.

types.embedding_query_text: Building: A structure with a roof and walls, such as a house, school, or factory. Also called Structure, Edifice, Premise. Examples: WHO headquarters.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentBuilding
chosen_type.justification: The 'WHO headquarters' is a building housing an intergovernmental organization, making 'GovernmentBuilding' a specific and appropriate fit.

candidates.label: GovernmentBuilding
candidates.comment: A GovernmentBuilding is a civic structure that houses government operations or services. Also called public building, state edifice, official premises. Examples: city hall, parliament building, courthouse, post office. Distinct from GovernmentOffice, which is a specific type of organization within a government building.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CivicStructure
candidates.comment: A public structure or building intended for public use or government functions. Also called public building, municipal structure, community facility. Examples: A library, a concert hall, a town hall, a park.

types.embedding_query_text: City: A large and densely populated urban area. Also called Metropolis, Town, Urban center. Examples: Geneva, Kisangani, Kinshsasa.

chosen_type.label: City
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'City' directly matches the Schema.org 'City' class, and all mentions are instances of cities.

candidates.label: City
candidates.comment: A large and permanent human settlement, typically an administrative area with a defined government. Also called town, municipality, urban area, metropolis. Examples: New York City, London, Tokyo, Paris. Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a broader category including states, provinces, etc.

candidates.label: Zoo
candidates.comment: A civic structure and facility where wild animals are housed, exhibited, and often bred for conservation and public education. Also called zoological garden, animal park, wildlife park. Examples: San Diego Zoo, London Zoo, Bronx Zoo.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: CityHall
candidates.comment: A government building serving as the administrative headquarters for a city or town. Also called town hall, municipal building, civic center. Examples: New York City Hall, London City Hall, a local town's municipal office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentPosition: An official role or office within a government. Also called Public office, Political role, Ministerial post. Examples: DR Congo's Health Minister.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentPosition
chosen_type.definition: An official role or office held by a person within a government or public administration.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate represents a governmental role or position; candidates are organizations, places, or declarations.

candidates.label: GovernmentDeclaration
candidates.comment: An official announcement or statement made by a government.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: PostOffice
candidates.comment: A PostOffice is a GovernmentOffice providing postal services. Also called postal service branch, mail office. Examples: USPS Post Office, Royal Mail sorting office, a local post office branch, a general post office.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

types.embedding_query_text: Month: One of the twelve periods of time into which a year is divided. Also called Calendar month. Examples: May.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: A named period of time corresponding to one of the twelve divisions of a year.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Month' directly matches the vocabulary 'Month' type, and 'May' is a perfect instance.

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: A named period of time corresponding to one of the twelve divisions of a year.

candidates.label: CalendarYear
candidates.comment: A specific calendar year.

candidates.label: CalendarSeason
candidates.comment: One of the four divisions of the year (spring, summer, autumn, and winter) marked by particular weather patterns and daylight hours.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A period of time defined by a start and end date, or a duration relative to a specific date.

types.embedding_query_text: EmergencyDeclaration: An official announcement by an authority that a state of emergency exists. Also called Emergency decree, State of emergency. Examples: public health emergency.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentDeclaration
chosen_type.definition: An official announcement or statement made by a government.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'EmergencyDeclaration' is best captured by 'GovernmentDeclaration', as it refers to an official announcement by an authority.

candidates.label: GovernmentDeclaration
candidates.comment: An official announcement or statement made by a government.

candidates.label: SpecialAnnouncement
candidates.comment: A date-stamped textual information update from a locally-oriented organization, often related to urgent crisis situations, including contextual web links and structured data. Also called public notice, crisis update, community alert, emergency announcement. Examples: a school closure announcement due to weather, a pharmacy's updated operating hours during a pandemic, a local government's public health advisory.

candidates.label: EmergencyService
candidates.comment: An EmergencyService is a LocalBusiness providing immediate assistance in urgent situations. Also called emergency response, crisis service. Examples: A fire station, an emergency room, a police department, an ambulance service.

candidates.label: Disaster
candidates.comment: A sudden event, such as an accident or a natural catastrophe, that causes great damage or loss of life.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A particular day, month, and year, or a specific point in time. Also called Calendar date, Day, Timepoint. Examples: 1 July, Earlier this week.

chosen_type.label: TemporalExpression
chosen_type.definition: A phrase or term that refers to a specific point or period in time, which may be absolute or relative.
chosen_type.justification: Neither 'Date' nor 'DateRange' fully encompasses both specific dates ('1 July') and relative temporal expressions ('Earlier this week').

candidates.label: CalendarYear
candidates.comment: A specific calendar year.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A period of time defined by a start and end date, or a duration relative to a specific date.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: AnimalSpecies: A group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of exchanging genes or interbreeding. Also called Fauna, Animal type. Examples: fruit bats.

chosen_type.label: Taxon
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'AnimalSpecies' is well-represented by 'Taxon', which is defined to include species and biological classifications like 'fruit bats'.

candidates.label: Animal
candidates.comment: A living organism that feeds on organic matter, typically having specialized sense organs and nervous system and able to respond rapidly to stimuli.

candidates.label: Taxon
candidates.comment: A cohesive biological unit representing a group of organisms, such as a species, genus, or family. Also called biological classification, taxonomic group, species, genus. Examples: Homo sapiens, Canis familiaris, Felidae (cat family), Plantae (plant kingdom).

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: VeterinaryCare
candidates.comment: A local business or organization providing medical services for animals. Also called vet clinic, animal hospital, veterinary practice. Examples: a local veterinary office, an emergency animal hospital, a mobile vet service.

candidates.label: AnimalShelter
candidates.comment: An AnimalShelter is a LocalBusiness that provides temporary housing and care for animals, often facilitating adoption. Also called animal rescue, humane society, pet shelter. Examples: The ASPCA, a local humane society, a dog rescue organization.

types.embedding_query_text: Province: A principal administrative division of certain countries or empires. Also called Region, State, Territory. Examples: South Kivu, North Kivu, Ituri, Tshopo province.

chosen_type.label: State
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Province' directly matches the Schema.org 'State' class, which explicitly includes 'province' in its definition.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: AdministrativeArea
candidates.comment: An AdministrativeArea is a geographical region, typically governed by a specific authority. Also called political division, jurisdiction, governmental region, territory. Examples: A country, a state, a province, a city, a county.

candidates.label: DefinedRegion
candidates.comment: A geographic area defined by specific, potentially non-administrative criteria, such as a set of postal codes or states. Also called Custom region, service area, delivery zone, sales territory. Examples: "All US states except Alaska and Hawaii", "Postal codes 90210-90215", "The greater London area for delivery". Distinct from AdministrativeArea, which is a politically defined region like a state or county.

candidates.label: SchoolDistrict
candidates.comment: An administrative area responsible for the organization and operation of public schools within its geographical boundaries. Also called education district, school system, local education authority. Examples: 'Los Angeles Unified School District', 'New York City Department of Education', 'Springfield School District 186'.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsAgency: An organization that gathers news reports and sells them to subscribing newspapers, periodicals, and broadcasters. Also called Press agency, Wire service. Examples: Reuters, AFP.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'NewsAgency' directly matches the Schema.org 'NewsMediaOrganization' class, which explicitly lists 'news agency' as an alias.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: InsuranceAgency
candidates.comment: An InsuranceAgency is a financial service local business that provides insurance-related services. Also called insurance broker, insurance provider, insurance firm. Examples: State Farm, Geico, a local independent insurance agent.

candidates.label: ReportageNewsArticle
candidates.comment: A ReportageNewsArticle is a NewsArticle representing news articles based on factual journalistic reporting, emphasizing verified information and multiple viewpoints. Also called news report, journalistic article, factual news. Examples: a breaking news story about a political event, an investigative report on a social issue, a factual account of a natural disaster, a report on scientific findings. Distinct from AnalysisNewsArticle, which goes deeper into analysis.

candidates.label: NewsArticle
candidates.comment: A NewsArticle, as an Article, is a creative work whose content reports news or provides background context for understanding news. Also called news report, news story, journalistic article. Examples: a breaking news report, an investigative journalism piece, an opinion column in a newspaper. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically less formal and often personal.

types.embedding_query_text: Duration: The length of time that something continues or exists. Also called Period, Span, Length of time. Examples: two to 21 days, weeks.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Duration' directly matches the Schema.org 'Duration' datatype, which represents periods of time.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Month
candidates.comment: A named period of time corresponding to one of the twelve divisions of a year.

candidates.label: DateRange
candidates.comment: A period of time defined by a start and end date, or a duration relative to a specific date.

candidates.label: CalendarYear
candidates.comment: A specific calendar year.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

types.embedding_query_text: Facility: A place, amenity, or piece of equipment provided for a particular purpose. Also called Establishment, Premises, Site. Examples: laboratories.

chosen_type.label: Laboratory
chosen_type.definition: A facility equipped for scientific research, experiments, or testing.
chosen_type.justification: 'Place' is too broad, and no existing candidate captures the specific meaning of a 'laboratory' as a type of facility.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: Room
candidates.comment: A distinguishable space within a structure, typically separated by interior walls. Also called chamber, compartment, space, area. Examples: a hotel room, a living room, a bedroom, a conference room.

candidates.label: Accommodation
candidates.comment: An Accommodation is a Place that can house human beings, such as a hotel room, camping pitch, or meeting room. Also called lodging, dwelling, living space, temporary residence. Examples: A hotel suite, a campsite, a vacation rental apartment, a conference room.

candidates.label: House
candidates.comment: A House is an accommodation type representing a building or structure intended for human or other creature habitation. Also called dwelling, residence, home. Examples: a single-family home, a townhouse, a cottage. Distinct from Apartment, which is a unit within a larger building, and HotelRoom, which is a temporary lodging unit.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

types.embedding_query_text: GovernmentAgency: A permanent or semi-permanent organization in the machinery of government responsible for the oversight and administration of specific functions. Also called Public body, State agency. Examples: US public health authorities.

chosen_type.label: GovernmentOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'GovernmentAgency' directly matches the Schema.org 'GovernmentOrganization' class, which explicitly includes 'agency' in its definition.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: TravelAgency
candidates.comment: A local business that assists individuals and groups in planning and booking travel arrangements. Also called travel agent, tour operator, booking agency. Examples: Expedia, a local independent travel agency, a corporate travel management company.

candidates.label: GovernmentOffice
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOffice is a local business representing a specific governmental agency or department. Also called public agency office, state department branch, municipal service center. Examples: IRS office, DMV office, local planning department, social security office. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is the physical structure that may contain multiple offices.

candidates.label: GovernmentService
candidates.comment: A GovernmentService is an intangible service provided by a government organization to the public. Also called public service, state-provided service, municipal offering. Examples: food stamps program, veterans benefits, public education, waste collection.

candidates.label: EmploymentAgency
candidates.comment: An EmploymentAgency is a LocalBusiness that helps individuals find jobs and employers find suitable candidates. Also called recruitment agency, staffing firm, job placement service. Examples: A temporary staffing agency, an executive search firm, a headhunting company.

types.embedding_query_text: RebelGroup: An organized group that resists the government or ruling power. Also called Insurgent group, Militant group, Guerrilla group. Examples: M23 rebel group.

chosen_type.label: RebelGroup
chosen_type.definition: An organized group that resists the government or ruling power, often through armed conflict.
chosen_type.justification: No existing candidate captures the specific meaning of a 'rebel group' as an organization resisting government, distinct from a political party.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: NationalGroup
candidates.comment: A group of people sharing a common nationality.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: PoliticalParty
candidates.comment: A PoliticalParty is an Organization formed to contest elections and hold power in government. Also called political movement, party. Examples: Democratic Party, Republican Party, Labour Party, Conservative Party.
